industry.ipm: The Indian pharmaceutical market (IPM) was ~₹2.15 lakh crore at chemist level in FY26 (IQVIA SSA MAT Mar-26; cardiac ₹30,287 cr = 14.1%) and grew 9.0%; growth rose to 12.2% in the Jun-2026 quarter (acute 10.1%, chronic 15.4%), helped by generic semaglutide after its Mar-2026 patent expiry. Alkem's four biggest therapies are acute and grew slowly market-wide in FY26: anti-infectives +4.0%, gastro +5.7%, pain +7.2%, VMN +9.2%; the fast lanes were cardiac +13.8%, anti-diabetic +11.5% and respiratory +11.3%.

themes: Chronic grows ~1.2-1.5x acute; Alkem's chronic share is ~22-23% of branded sales and rises ~1pp a year (CEO, Q4FY26 call), so most of Alkem sits in the slower half.
The category grew only 4% in FY26; oral liquids and injectables struggled (CEO). Alkem is #1 with a 13% share: leadership in a slow market.
Alkem launched on day one (Mar-2026) and is top-3 among generics, but the contribution is 'very small' (MD, Aug-2026); prices are falling fast.
Alkem is #1-2, but 'a lot of big guys have entered' (MD); growth ~4% in FY26 and flat in Q1FY27 as Alkem tightened credit.

Scheduled drugs rise only with WPI; many old acute molecules are scheduled. The Uniform Code for Pharmaceutical Marketing Practices (2024) restricts gifts and sponsored travel for doctors; GST on most medicines was cut to 5% from Sep-2025.
Volume growth absent in new launches; price erosion 'bottomed out' (MD); Indian plants face rising USFDA scrutiny (Alkem's Daman OAI).
US buyers want non-Chinese biologics capacity, but 'big companies take a lot of time' and are building their own (MD, May-2026).

moat: Acute brands and anti-infectives leadership
Strong
#1 in anti-infectives for 15+ years (13.3% share); Pan family #2 in the IPM (₹1,000 cr+ brand family); Clavam #9; 17 brands above ₹100 cr = 52% of domestic sales.
Real and durable, but the categories grow 4-9% a year: leadership in slow lanes.
Reach: field force and trade generics
Moderate
14,500+ reps (attrition 18-19%), #3 by prescriptions; #1-2 in trade generics with a direct distributor network.
Scale matters, but trade generics is a price game that bigger rivals have now entered.
Chronic franchise
Weak
~22-23% of branded sales; rank #13 in anti-diabetic, #14 respiratory, #19 derma, #8 CNS.
Growing 1.2-1.6x the market from a small base; no position of strength yet.
US generics
None
192 ANDAs filed, no volume growth in recent launches; Daman (45% of US sales) under OAI.
A price-taker business; no moat, and regulatory risk is live.
Biosimilars and CDMO (Enzene)
Unproven
8 biosimilars in India (~₹150 cr, profitable); EMA approval for denosumab; US CDMO loses ~₹240 cr a year before revenue.
Option value; outsiders priced Enzene at ~₹2,800 cr (Feb-2026).
Cost and tax position
Eroding
Sikkim tax-holiday units cut the tax rate to 12-18% for a decade; that ends in FY27 (30-32%).
A ~13pp tax step-up is a permanent EPS reset, not a cycle.
critiques: EPS falls in FY27 on tax alone: the Sikkim holiday ends and the consolidated rate jumps from 18% to 30-32%, so FY27E EPS is below FY26 on our numbers despite ~10% EBITDA growth.
Alkem's core is acute, and acute is the slow half of the market (anti-infectives +4% in FY26); 'outperformance' of 100-200bp still means low-teens growth at best.
The new businesses burn cash before they earn it: Enzene US (~₹240 cr opex a year, breakeven only at $25-30mn of sales in FY28), Occlutech (breakeven EBITDA in FY27), ortho MedTech (losses).
Daman's OAI covers ~45% of US sales; supplies continue, but new approvals from the site are likely to be held until it is cleared.

Governance: six promoter-family executive directors; KMP and relatives took ~₹135 cr in FY26 (~5.9% of profit); a Sep-2023 tax search with press reports of doctor payments; the professional CEO left after ~3 years.
Promoters keep selling (55.1% → 49.7% in five quarters), which caps the stock on rallies.
Treasury money in non-core assets: a ₹75 cr impairment on real-estate investments in Q4FY26.
The street splits 21x (BOBCAPS) to 27x (MOSL) and its targets sit around today's price; only ICICI Securities (Buy, May-2026) sees big upside.
